newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel reform to up ceiling on investment abroad.
newsitem.headline: Israel reform to up ceiling on investment abroad.

text.p: The foreign currency reform announced on Tuesday will increase the amount institutional investors and businesses can invest abroad, Treasury and Bank of Israel sources said.
The ceiling on overseas investment for institutionals would rise to five percent of assets from the current two percent.
At the same time taxes on real capital gains from overseas investments, currently at 35 percent, would be lowered though by how much has not yet been decided.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frekel and Finance Minister Dan Meridor also agreed to gradually raise the amount businesses can invest overseas.
A proposal by the Bank of Israel to allow Israelis to open dollar accounts in Israeli banks was rejected, the sources said.
A budget cut was also agreed although the size of the reduction was not finalised. The sum of 600 million shekels was discussed but not decision was reached, the sources said.
The three will continue talks on Tuesday afternoon in Jerusalem on the issue of widening the shekel's trading bands.
